caption:
When Notre Dame’s Ethan Long came lookin’ for custom gear, we didn’t hand out stickers and cheap foam caps…no, we fired up the laser, fed the Mauser sewing machine, and built artifacts that smell like burnt leather and big hits on third down.

Two one-off leather patch hats, stitched on the Mauser post-bed till the bench begged for mercy. Each patch carries his own autograph, burned deep into full-grain hide. Not printed. Not pressed. Etched in.

Then we dropped a laser-engraved tumbler…blue and gold, same colors that roar under the South Bend lights. And because legends don’t toss their gear in plastic, we finished it with a custom leather-patch cotton drawstring bag to carry it all.

This isn’t merch.
This is legacy..scorched, stitched, and sealed in grit.

#EngravedCo #NotreDame #EthanLong #LeatherPatchHats #LaserEngravedTumbler #MadeInIndiana #PostBedPower #notredamefootball #NDvsUSC

So thank you to all of the people that were there to support me love on me and keep my light shining. Lots of ups and downs and lots of time to get better and evaluate where I am in life. caption:
Still taking it all in. 🙏🏽 Grateful to have been invited to the Next Gen Camp led by @jlin7 and his incredible team — a space built for us, by us.
Being surrounded by some of the top Asian athletes from across the country reminded me: we’re out here. We’re growing. And we’re only getting louder. 🗣️ This camp wasn’t just about basketball — it was about building something bigger. A community. A culture. A reminder that we belong in these spaces too.
Getting hands-on experience and insight from someone I’ve looked up to for years was unreal. From deep convos off the court to competing with some of the best, it was everything I didn’t know I needed.
I’ll say this — it’s different when you’re learning from people who look like you, get you, and want to see you win.
Would do it all over again for the people, the purpose, and the chance to help build what’s next. 🏀🌏 #representationmatters #nextgencamp #asianathlete #basketballculture #basketballcommunity #hoopdreams

Everything happens for a reason. 

6 months ago, I started my road to recovery. This journey has been far from easy but has shown me the importance of having patience, understanding good things take time, and realizing who’s in my corner. I’ve learned to define success on my personal growth rather than a timeline. Surrounding myself with people who truly care about my wellbeing as a person and athlete has given me so much reassurance and belief in myself.  This temporary setback has changed how I see myself and challenged me have patience and trust that God has a plan perfectly designed for me. I am confident in where I am as I move through recovery and where I will be at the end of this. I’m so thankful for the team of people I have around me who challenge me to be my best everyday!

caption:
Dear travel softball, 

Thank you for the unforgettable memories, you were more than just part of a sport to me. You’ve taught me what it means to be a leader you’ve given me strength and most of all you have given me my best friends. I can’t thank you enough for the friendships you have given me. I never knew what it felt like to have a group of girls to call my own and I am so blessed I was able to experience true friendship over the years.  I would do anything to play one more game with these girls who truly changed my life. Coach Steve did a great job picking out my future bridesmaids and I couldn’t be more thankful for that. Thank you to Coach Steve for being the head coach I always needed and always believing in me even when I didn’t believe in myself. Lastly, Thank you to my dad for being there every step of the way and making sure I had every tool I needed to succeed. I am going to miss our late night hitting sessions the most. As I close this chapter, I do so with a full heart. Travel softball gave me more than I could have ever imagined. Every little aspect shaped me into who I am today. 

With love,
Hayden Kyne

caption:
As I am wrapping up my last off season playing the sport I love, I can only reflect on all it has taught me. The journey of being an athlete at the highest level is filled with challenges that often go unnoticed. From the pressures, expectations and dissatisfaction you and others impose on yourself, it can feel beyond overwhelming at times. The privilege of being a student-athlete is undeniable, yet the reality is that it demands so much of us. These struggles can lead to losing sight of who we are in the process.

Every ache and pain in your body tells a story of hard work and dedication. There are days when you may feel invincible, but then there are those days when it feels like the weight of the world is on your shoulders. On top of that, the mental battles are just as tough, if not worse, than the physical ones. It’s important to recognize that not every day is the same; some days are filled with victories, while others are marked by frustration and doubt. 

However, we often forget that behind every successful athlete is a story of perseverance and grit.

Through it all, we are strong. We have shown resilience and determination that is truly inspiring. Each time we step onto the court, we carry not just our hopes, but the hopes of those who came before us. We break barriers and set examples for the next generation of female athletes. You should be proud of the person you’ve become, as nothing defines you except for your own perception of yourself. Remember, the little girl who dreamed big and worked hard is still within you. She is still in you, and she deserves to shine brightly, no matter the challenges that come your way. Embrace every moment, for they are all part of your incredible journey. 

I’ve got one more season to make a mark on a program that has given me everything. I am proud of the girl I once was, and am even more proud of the woman I have become. Look in the mirror and tell yourself that. You deserve it. 

Love Thee. 💚

As I reflect on this season, I would like to thank everyone who was apart of this journey. I am very grateful for all of the memories and people that I’ve met this year.
To the Senior class, I have been blessed to be able to play alongside you for the last three years. We have shared many laughs, stories, and accomplishments that we will remember forever. Thank you, Seniors. 
To my teammates, I am beyond proud of what we have accomplished. Thank you for being there through the highs and the lows, I could always count on you guys to be there. There were many late nights and early mornings that were put into accomplishing this goal, and I am proud of how hard we worked to make it happen. When everyone counted us out, we continued to bet on ourselves and believed in ourselves. The bonds we created are inseparable and remarkable. You guys are my brothers forever.
To the coaching staff, thank you for pushing us to be better, day in and day out. Your dedication to this team and program is unmatched. You have taught us what it takes to be successful, how to bounce back when faced with adversity, and to always respect the game. 
To the Penn community, thank you for the unwavering love and support. Your cheers and words of encouragement have not gone unnoticed. We are blessed to have such a passionate and caring community behind us. 
Until next year 💛

I want to thank my family: Mom, Dad, Kevin, Jules, and Grace for always being there for me and helping me along the way. I would also like to thank all the other schools who have recruited me along this process— it’s been a humbling experience and I am very grateful.
